purpose: Fresh prospective controls for validating a selective-memory cognition amendment after the burned saturated baseline. These cases were not used to design or score the baseline.

places.description: A public secondary school with classrooms, lockers, a cafeteria and project rooms.
A modest family apartment with shared kitchen and living spaces.
A public library with open shelves, printers and study tables.
A familiar neighborhood bus and tram network used for school and errands.
A neighborhood community center with workshops and multipurpose rooms.
A walkable neighborhood street with shops, crossings and transit stops.

world.householdShape: Two caregivers, the subject and one younger sibling share the same apartment.
familyRelations: The younger sibling is three years younger than the subject.
world.materialCircumstances: Housing and ordinary expenses are stable; discretionary spending is limited.
world.mobilityPattern: School and local errands use walking and public transit.
world.schoolingOrCommunityContext: Public school, library, community center and neighborhood transit structure ordinary routines.
world.culturalContext: A mixed urban neighborhood with ordinary family, school and peer routines.
world.intellectualEnvironment: Books, school projects, practical workshops and ordinary family discussion are available without a prescribed worldview.

baselineBinding.observed: strong residue remembered 4/4; ordinary non-selection 0/4; matched-pair separation 0/4; provider-free replay exact

decisionRule.interpretation: Development proof only. The correction passes only if both retention and non-selection are exercised on fresh controls; no quota forces any individual decision and no valid output is resampled for quality.

history.observableAction: The child opened the assigned locker after class, moved a coat and two books into a backpack, and walked to the bus stop.
The child discovered the locker key was missing shortly before the last bus, retraced the hallway and cafeteria, found it under a bench, and reached the stop just before departure.
The child set four places at the dinner table, carried water glasses from the kitchen, and put the placemats away after the meal.
A smoke alarm sounded while a caregiver was outside; the child turned off the stove, took the younger sibling into the hallway, and waited there until the caregiver returned.
The teenager used the library printer for a school worksheet, stapled the pages, returned the print card, and left for home.
The teenager realized a school notebook with months of work had been left beside the library printer, returned before closing, and found it where it had been set down.
A winter route closure sent the teenager to an unfamiliar interchange; after checking the posted map, the teenager found an alternate bus home.
The teenager boarded the usual bus after school, listened for the familiar stop announcement, and walked the normal route home.

priorMemories.rememberedContent: I remember the route closure and working out an unfamiliar interchange to get home.

history.observableAction: A class project display collapsed before presentation; the teenager and a classmate rebuilt the frame during lunch and presented it that afternoon.
The teenager washed the dinner dishes, dried the counter, and put the dish towel over the oven handle before going to another room.

priorMemories.rememberedContent: I remember rebuilding the collapsed project display with a classmate before the presentation.

history.observableAction: During a workshop demonstration, the teenager's first circuit failed; after tracing a loose connection, the teenager repaired it and completed the demonstration.
The teenager wiped down a worktable after a community-center workshop, returned borrowed tools to labeled drawers, and left when cleanup ended.
